angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,443,990 km at 124.22 pc = 0.8 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 33579: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 8.05 +/- 0.14 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1134/S1063773712050015): 124.224 +/- 2.16 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 10.7 +/- 0.69 solar radii from Computed here, not printed by a paper: 10.7 +/- 0.69 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.8 +/- 0.05 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 8.05 +/- 0.14 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/167.1.121): 7,443,990 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 20990 +/- 760 K from Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 52089: effective temperature 20990 +/- 760 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 52089: effective temperature 20990 +/- 760 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.5 from 2025ApJ...979...21S; the 6 published values span log g 3.29 to 3.65, across which the limb law changes by at most 1.8% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJ...979...21S)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps CMa: spectral type B1.5II (2024A&A...690A.176N)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps CMa: main object type *, Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eps CMa: projected rotation speed 26 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2024A&A...687A.228D)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 52089) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
